memory_update.text: LOPE should remain a reference anchor for hybrid ABSN/OTA capacity because its disclosed hybrid pillar, partner university programs, simulation/VR investment and prerequisite strategies map directly to the node.

ATGE should remain a reference anchor for healthcare workforce education, especially Chamberlain nursing and Walden healthcare/social-work/mental-health programs, but requires regulatory and student-outcome checks in later layers.

HSTM is a promising underfollowed supplier hypothesis: healthcare workforce SaaS may hide clinical-placement, credentialing, competency and continuing-education exposure relevant to scarce healthcare-training capacity.
CAE is an underfollowed equipment/simulation hypothesis: aviation and defense labels may obscure healthcare simulation exposure to medical and nursing schools.

Need a focused later pass on private or non-US-listed simulation suppliers and clinical-placement software vendors, because several likely bottleneck suppliers may not be US-listed or may be embedded inside broader companies.

node: Hybrid healthcare education capacity: ABSN, OTA, nursing, counseling, social work, simulation, and clinical infrastructure
summary: Layer 1B expands the universe around the capacity-constrained healthcare-education node. The strongest direct public-market anchors are Grand Canyon Education and Adtalem, which own or service hybrid/healthcare education capacity. The more underfollowed supplier lane points to HealthStream for healthcare workforce learning, credentialing, competency, scheduling and clinical-exchange software, and CAE for simulation/VR/immersive medical-training infrastructure. Evidence strength is highest for direct program exposure at LOPE and ATGE; HSTM and CAE are better chokepoint hypotheses because they sit one step away from enrollment demand and may benefit if schools and healthcare employers need more scalable clinical training, simulation, credentialing, and workforce infrastructure.
